canon_standing.math_library: PARTIALLY_COMPUTABLE — pack serves pe, peg, fwd_peg, p_b, p_s, p_fcf, debt_to_equity, margins, dividend_yield. C8 (Lynch PEG), C12 (equity ratio, derived as 1/(1+D/E)) and C13 (FCF yield, derived as 1/p_fcf) ARE testable this run. C10/C11 (net cash floor, effective P/E) remain NOT_COMPUTABLE — no cash or net-cash-per-share field.
canon_standing.category: NOT_SERVED — no lynch_category field. Six-category placement (C5, C6) is inferred nowhere; where I name a category read below it is PROVISIONAL from margin/yield/leverage shape only and carries no verdict on its own.
canon_standing.fail_gates: NOT_TESTABLE — Gate 1 (bank vs funded debt with <12m maturities) needs the debt KIND split (C15): absent. Gate 2 (inventory growth vs sales growth, two consecutive quarters) needs inventory + revenue series (C14): absent. Gate 3 (Fast Grower PEG>2.0 OR institutional ownership >75%) is half-testable — PEG is served, institutional ownership is not. No gate is reported PASS; an untested gate is never a pass.
canon_standing.two_minute_drill: NOT_POSSIBLE (C3) — no business description, product, segment or expansion data in the pack. Every verdict below is a RATIO verdict, not a story verdict.
canon_standing.peg_methodology_caveat: FMP peg is trailing and FMP-computed. A NEGATIVE PEG means the growth denominator is negative (earnings declining), NOT a bargain. Seven names carry negative trailing PEG (CNH, DE, LNG, KHC, SLB, CTVA, BOX) and five carry negative forward PEG (KHC, EQT, CVX, UMC, PBR). I read every negative PEG as an earnings-decline signal, never as PEG<0.5 bargain territory (C8).
canon_standing.stop_position: DEFERRED_TO_HOUSE_LAW (C21 pm_override) — I take no position on any bracket, stop or risk gate.

fundamentals_judgment.rationale: Price is miles ahead of the earnings, on both the trailing and the forward read: pe 124.59, peg 15.93, fwd_peg 9.37 — the forward figure is still ~4.7x Lynch's 2.0 overvalued red-flag line (C8), so this is not a stale-trailing-earnings artefact. p_s 13.74 and p_fcf 65.09 (FCF yield ~1.5%) sit far below the 5% CapEx-heavy fail line (C13). Balance sheet is the one comfortable part — debt_to_equity 0.42 gives an equity ratio of ~70%, short of C12's 75% sound mark but nowhere near leveraged, and altman_z 4.54 is safe zone. piotroski 5 is middling. dividend_yield 1.28 does not rescue a 124x multiple (C9). Provisional category note: the ratio shape is what a REIT looks like through GAAP EPS, where depreciation buries earnings and FFO is the operative metric — the pack serves no FFO, so I flag the distortion and DO NOT excuse the multiple on it.
red_flags: peg 15.93 and fwd_peg 9.37 both far above the 2.0 overvalued line
FCF yield ~1.5% — below the 5% fail threshold (C13)
GAAP-EPS multiple likely distorted by REIT depreciation; no FFO/AFFO served to test it

fundamentals_judgment.rationale: The valuation read is a cyclical read, not a growth read. peg -0.81 is NOT a bargain — the denominator is negative — and pe 50.26 on net_margin_pct 1.71 is the classic trough-earnings/high-multiple signature. fwd_peg 1.08 is the one respectable number. What stops me is the balance sheet: debt_to_equity 3.39 puts equity ratio at ~23% and debt at ~77%, deep past C12's 50% line, and altman_z 1.95 sits barely above the 1.8 distress boundary. piotroski 7 and p_fcf 13.0 (~7.7% FCF yield) argue the other way, p_s 0.85 is genuinely low. The decisive question I cannot answer is C15 — how much debt is bank debt callable on short notice vs funded bonds — and for a capital-goods maker with a captive finance arm the raw D/E is not comparable to an industrial peer's.

altman_z 1.95, one notch above distress

asks: lynch_category field (Slow Grower / Stalwart / Fast Grower / Cyclical / Turnaround / Asset Play) — highest-leverage ask; half the verdicts rest on a PROVISIONAL category read inferred from margin/yield/leverage shape.
Explicit long-term earnings growth rate alongside PEG — 12 of 20 names carry a negative trailing or forward PEG; without the raw growth rate I cannot tell a mild decline from a collapse.
Cash and net-cash-per-share, to compute C10 net cash floor and C11 effective P/E — dark for AAPL and EQT, judged on a headline P/E Lynch would explicitly overrule.
Inventory and revenue for two consecutive quarters — decisive for CNH, DE, ADM, CTVA; Fail Gate 2 currently NOT_TESTABLE for all 20 names.
Long-term debt split by KIND — most important unserved field for GEN (Z 1.45), T (0.97), OKE (1.70), CNH (D/E 3.39), LNG (D/E 4.29).
Institutional ownership percentage — Fail Gate 3 half-testable on BOX and KVYO.
Payout ratio and dividend coverage — untestable on T, OKE, KHC (paying 6.18% against a TTM loss), PBR.
Sector-relative and own-history P/E context — could not run the Stalwart test on AAPL, DE or CVX.
USD-normalized market_cap and revenue for DB (EUR) and UMC (TWD) — currently uncomparable to USD peers.
Captive-finance-arm segmentation for DE (D/E 2.29) and CNH (D/E 3.39) — consolidated D/E conflates manufacturing and finance-receivable leverage.
REIT FFO/AFFO where applicable — WELL's pe 124.59 and peg 15.93 are GAAP-EPS artefacts of depreciation.
Process ask: the fundamentals pack should precede every CHALLENGE round, plus a one-line per-ticker business description so the Two-Minute Drill becomes partially answerable.
